title: Static methods and fields
learningObjectives: Explain static methods and fields and choose suitable object-oriented patterns.

understand.concept: Static methods and fields belong to the class constructor itself rather than individual instances. They are accessed through the class name. Static methods are useful for utilities or factory methods related to a class but not tied to one instance.
understand.whyItMatters: Static members help separate class-level operations from instance state. They should not be used as a global storage shortcut for unrelated mutable data.
understand.analogy: An instance member belongs to one item; a static member belongs to the shared class definition.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript object identity, prototypes, and class semantics are defined by the language.

explain.narrative: category and create are accessed on Course, while title belongs to the created instance.

practise.guidedTask: Add a static factory method that validates a title before creating an instance. Compare static and instance access.
practise.independentTask: Model a small domain using the simplest suitable object pattern. Explain the trade-offs between plain objects, functions, prototypes, and classes.
hints: Separate instance data from shared behaviour.
Check own properties and inherited properties.
Prefer composition when capabilities need to vary independently.

questions.explanation: Static methods are called on the class constructor itself.

questions.prompt: What should guide the choice between a plain object, function, and class?
options: The actual data and behaviour requirements
A rule that every object must be a class
The number of lines in the file name
questions.answer: The actual data and behaviour requirements
questions.explanation: Choose the least complex abstraction that clearly expresses the required behaviour.
